featured_reviews.review_text:
Gold coin Tardeo is located in the very popular area of south Mumbai. They got bright and positive vibes. Loved the bright lighting of the dining area. They got beautiful walls with a big chandelier in between. Seating has mainly couches so yes it is super comfortable.

The menu got excellent classic dishes. The bar has a few of the best cocktails and mocktails. The food menu got good variety available. Being an old and classical restaurant, their dishes were flavorful.

Cosmopolitan (Cocktail) – a classic cocktail made with vodka, sweet n sour, cranberry juice and orange liquor, served in a martini glass. (5/5)

Orange Mix Fizz (Mocktail) - A touch of basil and lime leaves, a fizzy drink made with orange bitters. Loved the balancing of flavors. (5/5)

Chakori Kebab – Chicken chunks marinated in green herbs, especially in fenugreek, then cooked well in tandoor. Loved the margination it was flavorful. (5/5)

Peri Peri Prawns – Prawns batter fried and tossed in peri peri sauce along with a few cubes of mix peppers. Loved the crunchiness of the prawns and the sauce was coated so well. (5/5)

Mutton Rogan josh – A classical dish made in the most authentic way. Boneless mutton cubes cooked so well in thin traditional rogan josh gravy. The Doneness of the mutton was too good. I had garlic butter naan with it, which was just perfect. (5/5)

Caramel custard- The best and my favorite dessert to try in a classic restaurant like this. It was superb.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Kanishka Veg Restaurant is a prominent pure vegetarian eatery situated in Mumbai, strategically located near iconic landmarks like the Mahalakshmi Temple and Haji Ali Dargah, making it a convenient dining spot for visitors exploring these spiritual sites. Nestled at 5-B, Haji Ali Circle, Tardeo Road, Mahalaxmi, the restaurant offers an inviting ambiance conducive for family dinners and casual meals alike.¹

Kanishka Veg Restaurant serves an array of delectable vegetarian dishes catering to diverse palates. *Authentic South Indian dishes* like _Sada Dosa_ and _Rava Masala Dosa_ are highlights, delivering *typical South Indian taste* that's true to regional flavors, complemented by flavorful chutneys that enhance the culinary experience. Patrons praise the *tasty dosa*, underscoring the restaurant's knack for capturing traditional essence.² ³

The restaurant boasts a *good atmosphere*, with interiors that are well-furnished and equipped with pleasant lighting, fostering a comfortable dining environment. Reviews highlight *good service*, with staff often described as attentive, friendly, and polite – essential for patrons seeking hassle-free dining, even during bustling festival periods like Diwali and Raksha Bandhan.⁴

Among popular items, diners specifically love *paneer tikka*, *kulcha*, *cheese pulav*, and *fried rice*, showcasing the kitchen's versatility across North Indian and Chinese-inspired vegetarian preparations. *Pav Bhaji* is another crowd-pleaser, available with options like Jain Pav Bhaji, reflecting accommodation for diverse dietary preferences.

On the beverage front, while the *chocolate shake is average*, visitors appreciate refreshing options like lassi – with one reviewer finding the lassi "definitely worth trying – refreshing and delicious!".

Kanishka Veg Restaurant offers a balanced mix of affordability and quality, with price ranges typically ₹200-₹400 per person, making it accessible for varied budgets. Cuisines span *South Indian*, *North Indian*, *Chinese*, *Fast Food*, and vegetarian staples, appealing to those craving familiar comfort food with vegetarian integrity.

Located opposite Haji Ali Juice Centre, proximity to spiritual hubs like Mahalakshmi Temple (0.3 km from Baskin-Robbins, another nearby eatery) and Haji Ali Dargah positions Kanishka Veg Restaurant as a practical choice for visitors blending devotion with gastronomy. Other nearby dining options include Cafe Noorani, McDonald’s Tardeo, and Haji Ali Juice Centre for those exploring alternatives.⁵

Operating hours stretch from *8 AM to 12 AM*, accommodating breakfast through late-night cravings.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Curry’s & Cocktails is a refreshing new addition to Ghatkopar’s dining scene, thoughtfully spread across three distinct sections. The ground level offers casual dining, perfect for family meals or catching up with friends. The next level is designed for intimate private parties, ideal for small groups, while the top floor transforms into a lounge bar with a live DJ, setting the mood for a lively evening.

We started with drinks, and the Achari Whiskey cocktail truly stood out — unique, bold, and packed with flavour.
For a non-alcoholic option, the Rising Sun mocktail, a refreshing blend of watermelon and pineapple juice, was light and delightful.

The appetizers didn’t disappoint. The Dahi ke Kebab was soft, creamy, and beautifully balanced, while the Chicken Tikka Balochi was medium spicy, well-chargrilled, and full of smoky goodness. A special mention goes to the Mumbai Patty Bao — a fun, creative take on street food, featuring a traditional Mumbai-style deep-fried potato patty tucked into a soft bao bun with onions, garlic chutney, lettuce, mint mayo, and fried salted green chillies.

For mains, we tried the Pink Lady Mee (Chicken). It was flavourful, vibrant, and nicely balanced.

Dessert was a pleasant surprise with the Shrikhand Crème Brûlée, blending classic Indian flavours with a modern twist — a perfect end to the meal.

Overall, Curry’s & Cocktails offers a lovely dining experience with good food, creative drinks, and versatile spaces to suit every mood — from relaxed family dinners to high-energy nights with music. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in or around Ghatkopar.

featured_reviews.name: aakruti dave
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Tripo Spice, a rooftop place with great ambience, ample seating space, and beautifully designed décor. The overall vibe is lovely and makes for a very pleasant dining experience.
We loved the food — the white sauce pasta was creamy and delicious, the dry Manchurian was flavourful, and the mint paneer was equally delicious. We also tried their special Belgium Brownie milkshake, which was super chocolaty and absolutely indulgent.
The staff is very courteous and polite, adding to the overall warm and pleasant experience.
The only downside was the seating policy — despite calling in advance, we were informed that weekend bookings are not accepted and only walk-ins are allowed. Additionally, they made us wait until all our friends had arrived before seating us, which felt a bit unnecessary.
Overall, it’s a wonderful family restaurant with good food, great ambience, and a well-designed rooftop setting. Definitely worth visiting for the food and ambience.

Highly recommended! 🌅✨

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place with my friends after hearing a lot about it, and it truly lived up to the expectations. We had a fantastic experience—both the food and the overall vibe were excellent.

We ordered Bombil fry as a starter, along with Prawns Thali and Surmai Thali. Every single dish was 10/10. Personally, whenever I try a new place for fish, I judge it by the taste of the Bombil fry—and this one was outstanding. It was extremely fresh, perfectly crispy, and the masala was well balanced and nicely blended.

The same quality and freshness reflected in the Surmai and Prawns thali—authentic taste and very satisfying portions.

On the owner’s suggestion, we also tried their Mutton Thali for a change, and it was surprisingly excellent. The mutton was fresh, tender, and full of flavour, which is rare to find these days.

If you’re a seafood lover, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy quality fish with great taste and vibes.
